title: ANCA-associated vasculitis
diseaseDescription: Bounded ANCA/neutrophil/complement and renal/pulmonary injury synthesis for GPA/MPA-spectrum AAV, with a separate EGPA context/view for eosinophils, extracellular traps, platelet-adhesion assays and ANCA-stratified heterogeneity. Human/culture/animal systems remain study-specific. Excludes drug-induced disease, comprehensive diagnostic/therapy coverage and general ANCA-negative GPA/MPA coverage; ANCA-negative EGPA is explicitly included.
releaseNote: Overall scientific summary of anca-associated-vasculitis-summary-candidate-eb8e14a28e3c; external current-literature review remains pending. Overall scientific summary of anca-associated-vasculitis-appraised-candidate-238031bf4b8a; external current-literature review remains pending. Provisional automatic appraisal of anca-associated-vasculitis-with-egpa-candidate-001. Automatic conservative metadata appraisal. Source entailment, study quality, broad disease coverage, circuit causation and independent replication require review. Confidence is capped at 1/4 until explicit editorial appraisal; therapeutic categories describe curated target coverage, not efficacy. No calibration or human approval is asserted. Independent review and calibration remain pending.

entities.label: MPO-ANCA
entities.description: Myeloperoxidase-reactive antibodies; mouse anti-MPO IgG experiments are distinct from human patient IgG.

entities.label: PR3-ANCA
entities.description: Proteinase-3-reactive patient IgG; not synonymous with all cytoplasmic-pattern ANCA.

entities.label: Neutrophils
entities.description: Human neutrophils used in the cited antibody/priming assays; experimental systems are retained per claim.

entities.label: TNF-alpha
entities.description: Tumour necrosis factor used to prime normal human neutrophils in the cited assay.

entities.label: Oxidative burst / degranulation
entities.description: Measured reactive oxygen species and primary-granule release from human neutrophils; not a clinical outcome.

entities.label: Alternative complement activation
entities.description: Complement pathway implicated by factor-B/C5 versus C4 knockout in an anti-MPO mouse model and by human serum assays.

entities.label: C5a
entities.description: Complement fragment produced in conditioned-serum experiments and used for neutrophil priming.

entities.label: Neutrophil extracellular traps
entities.description: Neutrophil-derived extracellular chromatin structures; tissue presence, culture generation and serum biomarkers are distinct findings.

entities.label: Renal inflammation / injury
entities.description: Here, necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis in anti-MPO mouse models and inflamed human kidney observations; claim-specific limits apply.

entities.label: Pulmonary capillaritis
entities.description: Hemorrhagic pulmonary capillaritis in the cited anti-MPO splenocyte-transfer mouse model, not a claim about purified-IgG lung injury.

entities.label: GPA/MPA-spectrum AAV activity
entities.description: Reported active/remission status and BVAS in selected human AAV cohorts; not a uniform activity measure across all AAV.

entities.label: Eosinophils
entities.description: Eosinophil counts, tissue eosinophils and eosinophil cultures measured in the EGPA reports; not interchangeable with neutrophils.

entities.label: Eosinophil extracellular traps
entities.description: Eosinophil-derived extracellular chromatin traps; distinct from neutrophil NETs.

entities.label: EGPA small-vessel thrombi
entities.description: Small-vessel thrombi containing lytic eosinophils/EETs in the selected EGPA tissue samples.

entities.label: Platelet adhesion
entities.description: Platelet adhesion to EET scaffolds assessed in vitro; not clinical thrombosis incidence.

entities.label: Circulating cell-free DNA
entities.description: Measured serum nuclear/mitochondrial cell-free DNA; not a cell-specific NET/EET measurement.

entities.label: EGPA disease activity
entities.description: Activity and treatment-associated changes in the small reported EGPA cohort.

entities.label: EGPA susceptibility
entities.description: Genetic susceptibility and ANCA-stratified disease features, distinct from current activity.

entities.label: EGPA patient serum
entities.description: Serum exposure from patients in remission used as an experimental input; not an identified pathogenic molecule.

limitations: Abstract-only inspection; full methods, controls, effect sizes and source-quality appraisal remain unverified.

claims.text: Purified anti-MPO IgG induced focal necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis in the reported mice.
limitations: Abstract-only inspection; full methods, controls, effect sizes and source-quality appraisal remain unverified.

claims.text: High-dose anti-MPO splenocyte transfer produced systemic vasculitis including hemorrhagic pulmonary capillaritis in the reported mouse model.
limitations: Abstract-only inspection; full methods, controls, effect sizes and source-quality appraisal remain unverified.
Experimental mouse anti-MPO model; does not establish every human GPA/MPA phenotype or PR3-ANCA pathogenicity.
Splenocyte-transfer finding; not proof that antibody alone caused the pulmonary lesion.

claims.text: ANCA-stimulated neutrophils released NETs containing PR3 and MPO in the reported experiments.
limitations: Abstract-only inspection; full methods, controls, effect sizes and source-quality appraisal remain unverified.

claims.text: Eosinophil extracellular traps were present in the examined EGPA small-vessel thrombi.
limitations: Abstract-only inspection; full methods, controls, effect sizes and source-quality appraisal remain unverified.

limitations: Abstract-only inspection; full methods, controls, effect sizes and source-quality appraisal remain unverified.

claims.text: Serum from patients in EGPA remission induced NET formation in healthy-donor neutrophils in vitro.
limitations: Abstract-only inspection; full methods, controls, effect sizes and source-quality appraisal remain unverified.

limitations: Abstract-only inspection; full methods, controls, effect sizes and source-quality appraisal remain unverified.
Human culture/serum assay; does not prove whole-disease causation or treatment efficacy.
Absence of a significant difference does not establish equivalence; subgroup differences described in the abstract remain material.

claims.text: Eosinophil number correlated with NET formation in the reported EGPA cohort.
limitations: Abstract-only inspection; full methods, controls, effect sizes and source-quality appraisal remain unverified.
Human association does not establish causal direction or comprehensive patient/organ coverage.

scientificSummary.scope: Selected MPO-/PR3-ANCA, neutrophil/complement and renal/pulmonary injury mechanisms for GPA/MPA-spectrum AAV, with a separate EGPA eosinophilic context. paragraphs.text: Within the selected GPA/MPA-spectrum evidence, patient MPO-ANCA and PR3-ANCA IgG activated human neutrophils in vitro, while TNF priming enhanced oxidative burst and degranulation. Activated-neutrophil supernatants activated serum complement and generated C5a; C5a then primed neutrophils for further ANCA responses. Together, these experiments support a context-bound amplification model, not proof of one universal disease circuit. Alternative-complement involvement is strengthened by protection of factor-B- and C5-deficient mice from anti-MPO renal disease. Purified anti-MPO IgG caused necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis in mice; pulmonary capillaritis was reported in the separate anti-MPO splenocyte-transfer experiment, not demonstrated here for antibody alone. ANCA-stimulated neutrophils also released NETs containing MPO and PR3, and NETs were observed in inflamed human kidneys. However, tissue presence does not prove disease initiation, and serum NET measurements in one human cohort did not reliably distinguish active disease from remission or correlate with BVAS and renal indices.

EGPA is represented separately rather than treated as an interchangeable ANCA-driven extension of that model. Its genetic study linked a tendency to eosinophilia with susceptibility and distinguished MPO-ANCA-positive from ANCA-negative subgroups. In selected EGPA tissue, lytic eosinophils and eosinophil extracellular traps were present in small-vessel thrombi; EETs supported platelet adhesion in vitro, but these findings do not establish the initiating cause of clinical thrombosis. In a small cohort, circulating cell-free DNA tracked activity only in the EGPA subgroup and was not shown to derive exclusively from EETs. Serum from patients in EGPA remission induced NET formation in healthy-donor neutrophils: the overall ANCA-positive/negative comparison was not significant, despite subgroup differences reported in the source. Eosinophil count correlated with NET formation without identifying the responsible serum factor. These culture, genetic and observational findings remain distinct from mouse experiments. Full methods, cohort independence, causal generality and contemporary literature completeness have not been established by this abstract-level curation. Therapy efficacy is outside this map; provisional automatic appraisals are uncalibrated, and independent domain and external summary review remain pending.
